tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on symptoms/user intent (job fails, times out, scores only part of its input, slow with idle instances, whether to use batch transform vs real-time endpoint), explicitly lists trigger contexts even when terms aren't named ('even if they do not mention JSON Lines, SplitType, MaxPayloadInMB...'), and while lengthy, remains a single cohesive paragraph focused on applicability rather than implementation.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a transform job fails with a parsing, content type, S3 access, bucket ownership, mount, capacity or internal server error, times out on large records, runs slowly with idle instances, reports success while output records are missing... even if they do not mention JSON Lines, SplitType, MaxPayloadInMB, ModelClientConfig, JoinSource, MaxConcurrentTransforms or KMS keys by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and domain-specific throughout — it describes SageMaker batch transform check-ids, severities, and routing logic without explaining generic concepts like what S3 or batch processing is. No filler or generic explanation is present.
tests.evidence: "Grounded in [checks-sagemaker-batch.md]... Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps detailed material (full check catalog, API quirks, known causes) in references/ and only presents a compact what-it-catches index table and a short router table in the body, pointing to references for details.
tests.evidence: "The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five reference files are linked via markdown links in the body (checks-sagemaker-batch.md, collection-reference.md, metrics-and-logs.md, api-quirks.md, known-causes.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a specific trigger condition for when to load it, e.g. tied to symptoms or check-ids in the router and other sections.
tests.evidence: "load it before assigning any check-id or severity" and "Load [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) whenever the user names an error or symptom"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference file links use relative paths in the format references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile sections (guardrails, check-id assignment, validation gate) are prescriptive with explicit non-negotiable rules, while flexible sections (break-fix answering, router usage) explain reasoning and allow judgment, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: "Non-negotiable, at every step: 1. Read-only. Never call a transform mutation..." vs "Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools/approaches as equal options; the router and check tables each point to a specific API/check without alternatives framed as equal choices.
tests.evidence: No menu-of-options language found; each router row specifies a single 'First read' API.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (symptom matching, check catalog, review steps) that applies to any batch transform job, rather than describing one specific instance's fix.
tests.evidence: "Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section and an 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious API quirks and misconceptions, serving as gotchas.
tests.evidence: "'The job is `Completed`, so every record was scored.' `Completed` means the job ran to the end... Reconcile with `ListObjectsV2` before clearing it"
